headline: SLOP WATCH ISSUED FOR THE LINKEDIN PLATEAU AND X BADLANDS AS FABRICATED-STATISTIC FRONT SCATTERS INVENTED PERCENTAGES, PHANTOM STUDIES, AND CONFIDENT DECIMAL POINTS CORRESPONDING TO NO SURVEY EVER CONDUCTED
advisory: A low-pressure system of unsourced numbers is drifting across the professional and commentary corridors, depositing precise-sounding figures with no measurable origin. Residents are advised that a statistic is not made true by the addition of a decimal point, and that the phrase 'studies show' is a weather condition, not a citation. The Service reminds the public that we too can generate a percentage on demand; we simply decline to pretend it means anything.

regional_outlook.conditions: Heavy accumulation of '87% of top performers do this one thing' posts, each figure holding steady at exactly one significant digit of plausibility. Traceable sourcing near zero through the evening.
Gusting phantom polls and 'a recent study found' fronts moving fast and citing nothing. Numbers expected to contradict one another by nightfall with no loss of confidence.
Fabricated statistics settling into featured snippets, where they will be quoted back by three further articles that also invented them. Circular sourcing likely.
Cold-outreach emails arriving with 'companies like yours see a 340% ROI' warnings. Denominator absent; expect flooding of the promotions folder.
Calm but persistent drizzle of infographics in which every wedge of every pie chart is labeled 'growth.' Visibility of methodology near nil.

specimen.status: Abundant; thriving in any habitat that rewards authority over accuracy.
specimen.habitat: Thought-leadership posts, cold emails, and the opening line of articles that need to sound researched.
specimen.field_marks: An oddly specific percentage — never a round number, always a 73% or a 4.2x — paired with the attribution 'studies show,' 'experts agree,' or the ever-migratory 'a recent report.' No report is ever named, linked, or found to exist.
specimen.call: Studies show that 87% of professionals who read this post will double their output by Thursday — and the top 1% already know why.
specimen.confusion_species: Easily mistaken for a genuine cited figure. Distinguish by following the source: a real statistic leads to a named survey, a sample size, and a date; the Phantom Statistic leads only to another post citing the same missing survey.

spotter_tip: If a figure ends in an exclamation point instead of a footnote, it was not measured — it was manufactured.
tomorrow: Tomorrow: fabricated figures weaken by midday as residents ask 'according to whom,' though isolated pie charts of pure 'growth' may linger through the afternoon.

confirmed_sighting.report: An empirical preprint documents the rise of AI-generated 'slop' tracks on music streaming services, analyzing how synthetic songs proliferate and reshape the streaming ecosystem — confirming that the slop tide now reaches beyond text and images into audio.
